mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Hyundai Tucson 1.6 Hybrid or PHEV engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Hyundai Tucson 1.6 Hybrid or PHEV engine typically costs between £3,500 and £6,500 supply-only, depending on the specific variant (HEV vs PHEV) and condition. Supply and fit labour typically adds £600-£1,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the Hyundai Tucson 1.6 Hybrid engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common issues include hybrid battery cooling system faults, electric motor bearing wear causing whining noises, and standard G4FP combustion engine issues like turbo wastegate sticking and intake valve carbon buildup.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai Tucson 1.6 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With a well-maintained Tucson 1.6 PHEV worth £18,000-£32,000, a £4,500-£6,500 specialist replacement engine is far more cost-effective than buying another used Tucson with the same underlying risks.

mainEntity.name: Can any garage fit a Hyundai Tucson 1.6 Hybrid engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Hybrid engine replacement requires specialist knowledge of high-voltage system isolation, ECU coding, and hybrid component calibration. Always use a hybrid-certified specialist for supply and fit.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a replacement Hyundai Tucson hybrid engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: All reconditioned and rebuilt Hyundai Tucson hybrid engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Extended 24-month warranties are available on premium rebuilt units.
